Start Before the first record

What it is

What the app does today:

  • Free. No ads and nothing to buy.
  • Your records stay on your phone unless you choose to keep them in an account as well.
  • You can take everything out: CSV for Excel or Google Sheets, JSON, Artisan and Cropster files for roasts, the EU plot file and Google Earth for plots.
  • Every tip names its source: a study, the Coffee Board, or common practice.
  • It works with no signal.
  • The app and its code belong to KoffyKraft; your records belong to you.

Seen fromRoast at a glanceNothing gets lostRecords you can trust

Watch out

Roast is not a certificate. It can check a plot against EU forest maps of 2020 and tree loss since, and gather what a European buyer asks for. That helps you get ready for the EU deforestation rule (EUDR). It does not certify anything and does not replace a lawyer, an auditor or the buyer's own checks.

Seen fromRoast at a glance

What it is

  • Not a guarantee. A drying time or a fermentation range is what a named source found, not a promise about your coffee.
  • Not a shop. Nothing is sold through it.
  • Not a judge of people. Records show who entered something, so it can be trusted or corrected. Nothing rates or ranks workers.
  • Not a place where mistakes vanish. A saved record is corrected, not deleted, and the change is kept beside it.

Seen fromRoast at a glanceRecords you can trust

Watch out

A few things ask a server and need the internet: signing in, the land check on a plot, and fetching weather. The app says so when it needs a connection; nothing you typed is lost.

Seen fromOn your phoneNothing gets lost

Tip

The language box puts the overviews and explanations into Malayalam, Kannada, Tamil, Spanish or Portuguese. Buttons, field names and numbers stay in English, so this manual still matches what you see.

Plot Where it grows

Watch out

A plot of 4 hectares or more needs its outline, not only a point: the plot says so in red. Buyers in Europe ask for the outline of large plots.

Seen fromEstates and plotsOne coffee, one chain

Step 5 · Check a plot against forest maps

With a location or outline saved, tap Run land check. The app compares the plot with the EU's map of forest at the end of 2020 and with tree loss since, and shows the result, the date and the sources. Each check is kept; the newest shows first.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 5One coffee, one chain

Watch out

The land check needs a signal and a signed-in account, and the app says so if either is missing. It is guidance for getting ready, not a certificate. If you change the outline later, the plot says the check describes the earlier shape, and offers Check again.

Seen fromEstates and plotsNothing gets lost

Step 7 · Record soil and how I care for it

Under Soil and soil life: the Soil type, the Texture (feel test), and a tick for each care practice you follow, such as mulch kept on the ground or little digging. Count Earthworms per spadeful if you like. Soil test results are rated against Indian Soil Health Card bands, and inputs applied keep their dates.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 7Quality as you go

Step 8 · Time backing and fruit drop

Under Flowering, give the Blossom shower date. The app works out when the backing shower is due (15 to 20 days after) and when fruit drop peaks (90 to 120 days after flowering), from CCRI figures. Add each flowering with + Add flowering.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 8Quality as you go

Step 12 · Read how to grow and pick

Crop care gathers tips on plant health, flowering, fruit set, berry borer and harvest, for Arabica, Robusta or Both, at Basic, Intermediate or Advanced level. Each tip names its source, mostly the Coffee Board and CCRI.

Try it in the app ›

Process run Cherry to green

Step 4 · Use a ready-made list of steps

Open Start from a ready-made protocol (optional) and pick one, such as Washed arabica, Indian estate (Coffee Board of India). You will see 7 steps added. Fill in times and weights as you go. Each step carries a short guide from that source.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 4Quality as you go

Step 8 · Take pH, Brix and temperature readings

Under Measurements, tap the measures you want for this step: Temp °C, pH, °Brix, Air °C, Air RH % and others, depending on the step. Each one shows a guide range. Tap + Reading now each time you measure; the time fills in, you type the numbers. With two readings or more, a small chart appears with the guide range shaded.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 8Quality as you go

Tip

Guide values and sources, after the last step, lists where each range comes from. They are starting points; sources differ, so adjust to your own lots.

Seen fromProcess runs

Step 9 · Ferment with a yeast or starter

In a Fermentation step, choose a method with a yeast or starter, such as With yeast / starter. An Inoculation box opens: pick the Product, type the Grams used, and if you like the rehydration water, its temperature and minutes, the price per kg and when it went into the tank. The product's notes, a suggested dose for the kilos in the step and how to rehydrate it come from the maker's published sheets.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 9Quality as you go

Green lot What goes to the roaster

Step 4 · Note moisture and grade

Under Quality, type the Moisture %. With no water activity meter, the app estimates it from moisture (10 to 13% only) and says whether it is good for storage; for robusta it adds that the estimate is rough, being worked out from arabica figures. Add Density g/L, Screen size, Grade, Cup score and where it is kept under Storage.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 4Quality as you go

Why it matters

Moisture and water activity decide how long green coffee keeps. The app's guide aims for 11 to 11.5% for long storage: above about 11.7%, water activity usually passes 0.61, and in a long Cafe Imports study lots above 0.61 lost more cup score in transit. A reading every few weeks shows a drift while there is time to act.

Seen fromGreen lotsQuality as you go

Passport What a buyer can check

What it is

The passport page says plainly what it proves: the entries were made by the phones shown, in this order, and have not been changed since the day they were stamped. What it cannot prove is that what was typed in was true. Honest records, photos and buyers who come back do that part.

Seen fromPassports and selling into EuropeRecords you can trust

What it is

The EU deforestation rule (EUDR) covers coffee sold into Europe. Each lot must come from land where no forest was cleared after 31 December 2020, must be grown under the country's laws, and must be traceable to the plots it grew on. The company that brings it into Europe files the due diligence statement; your part is to hand over complete, true records. The app's EUDR guide explains this in plain words.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromPassports and selling into EuropeOne coffee, one chain

Step 10 · See what a lot still needs for Europe

Open the green lot and tap EUDR. The app names any plot data still missing (a location, an outline) and holds the Product form, the HS code it suggests from the form, and the importer's statement reference once they file it.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 10One coffee, one chain

Step 12 · Make the EUDR lot file

From For a buyer, open the EUDR lot file: the lot, the product, quantity, when and where it was produced, the plots, the producer and the land check, on one page made from your records. Missing items show in red. Print or save as PDF to send it.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 12One coffee, one chain

What it is

The Legality pack puts the producer, land papers, licences, taxes and the team (as a count, never names or wages) on one page for a buyer, gathered from Origin, Land and dues, and Team and wages, with gaps shown. It lists what is recorded; it is not a certificate.

Roast Heat and time

Tip

Tick Drop guide for a guide to when to drop, worked out from the development time ratio (DTR).

Seen fromRoastingQuality as you go

Step 12 · Record roast colour

Open Colour and tap + New reading. Say what you measured (your roast, bought coffee, a sample), then type what your meter shows. With only a phone photo of ground coffee beside a white card, you get a ballpark roast level and Agtron, with how sure it is.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 12Quality as you go

Tip

Type every number your meter's screen shows. For meters with no published scale (ColorTrack, Colorette, Neotec), the app learns from your own paired readings. Each reading is shown on the other scales too, and named on three roast charts.

Seen fromRoastingQuality as you go

Cup Brew, cup and taste

Step 5 · Get closer to the cup I want

Under Dial in, pick where you want to go: Sweeter, Brighter, Fuller body, Less bitter or Cleaner. Or tell it What stands out in the cup?, such as sour, bitter or thin. It suggests what to change, from published findings and common practice, and Put the plan in Next time keeps the plan with the brew. If the section is not there, tick Show brew tips and dial-in help above it.

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 5Quality as you go

Watch out

The dial-in suggestions are guides, not guarantees, and the form says so. Your taste decides: brew again, rate it, and compare.

Seen fromBrewing and cupping

Step 6 · Learn how a brewer works

Brew guide explains each kind of brewer (drip and filter, espresso, moka pot, traditional, cold) at Basic, Intermediate or Advanced level, with step-by-step guides that run a timer and buzz at each step. Protocols are repeatable ways of working: a standard cup, measuring strength, dial-in, freshness, cold brew.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 6Quality as you go

Business People, work, sales, land

Step 8 · Keep land papers and dues

Open Land and dues. Land keeps each land record (survey number, area, ownership, documents). Tax and dues keeps land tax, insurance and loans with the next due date; record each payment when it is made. Licences keeps renewal dates. Due soon lists what falls due in the next 60 days.
